Reading the bounds

Each exact reported value is kept as a point. A retained left-censored result keeps its published interval; [0, 0.020) means a nonnegative mathematical lower bound and an excluded upper limit. Zero is not an observed concentration. Bounds describe the retained measurements, not a sampling confidence interval.

The equal-activity mean first averages the results within each original sampling activity, then gives each activity equal weight. The result-weighted mean gives every original result equal weight. Difference bounds use each same result in both means. Distinct original identifiers survive even when their reported values agree.

Separate source cohorts remain unchanged. Compatible measurement summaries require exact agreement on selected year, characteristic, fraction, quantitative unit inherited from the maintained interval, chemical basis, medium, activity type, both sampling depths and references, analytical method/context/name, result basis, time/weight/temperature/particle basis, statistical base, qualifier and status. Original unit and interval-unit provenance are retained as complete member sets within every compatible cohort. No chemical conversion, missing-depth substitution or cross-year pooling is performed.

2018 and 2024–2026 remain separate. The retained responses have no measurements in 2019–2023; no continuous trend, treatment effect, annual load or missing-day value is inferred. Arithmetic pH averages describe reported pH numbers and are not mean hydrogen-ion concentrations.
